name.en: Fake FBI “we recovered your money”: the second scam after the first

how.en: After someone has lost money to a scam, a person pretending to be from the FBI or its Internet Crime Complaint Center contacts them by email, phone or social media, or they see an ad or AI-generated video. They claim to have recovered the lost money or offer to help get it back, and send a link to “update your IC3 report” or a copy of the IC3 website. The real goal is to take more money or financial details from someone who has already been scammed.

text.en: After a scam, someone claiming to be the FBI or IC3 contacts you.
They say they recovered your money or can get it back.
They send a link to “update your report” on a fake IC3 site.
They ask for fees or financial details and take more money.

Hello, I am Special Agent R. Collins with the FBI IC3 recovery unit. We have recovered $18,400 linked to your complaint. To release the funds, update your report here and confirm your bank details: [link]

en: Someone offering to recover money you lost, especially for a fee.
An “FBI agent” on Facebook Messenger or Telegram.
A link to update an IC3 report that isn’t on ic3.gov.
The FBI never charges to recover money. Stop contact.
File reports only at ic3.gov, typed yourself.
Contact your bank if you shared financial details.

sources.title: FBI Warns of Scammers Impersonating the IC3
